eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader consensus in this Mexico City highest-temperature market centers on 24–26°C because climatological norms, the city’s high elevation, and current rainy-season conditions align closely with that narrow band.** Mexico City sits at roughly 2,240 m, where average August daytime maxima reach only about 24 °C; the urban heat-island effect and frequent afternoon convection limit further warming. Official forecasts for 11 August 2026 indicate a cloudy to overcast regime with late-day showers, keeping maximum temperatures near 23–25 °C (roughly 74–77 °F) and suppressing the chance of the 27 °C+ outliers priced below 3 %. Early-August observations showed brief spikes to 28–29 °C under clearer skies, yet persistent moisture and cloud cover since then have capped daily highs, reinforcing the market’s heavy weighting toward the 25 °C outcome (50.5 %). The slight edge to 25 °C over 24 °C or 26 °C reflects model consensus on modest afternoon clearing before convective development, with resolution hinging on the official Servicio Meteorológico Nacional or equivalent station reading at the end of the calendar day.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and official guidance point to a peak temperature of 38–39°C in Madrid on August 12, 2026, driving the heavy weighting toward those two outcomes.** AEMET’s municipal forecast lists a daily maximum of 38°C, with afternoon values reaching 35–36°C under mostly clear skies and light winds. International models align closely: BBC projects 38°C, while some guidance (timeanddate, AccuWeather monthly outlooks) edges toward 39°C amid strong insolation and the urban heat-island effect typical of central Spain’s continental climate.

**Key scientific drivers include persistent high pressure, minimal cloud cover, and dry northerly flow that limits cooling.** August climatology for Madrid shows average highs near 32–34°C, but current conditions reflect an extended warm spell with limited nocturnal recovery (overnight lows ~23–25°C). Low precipitation probability (<10–20%) and light winds further favor maximum realization of daytime heating. Minor model spread—some runs capping at 37°C while others reach 39°C—explains the 60.5% / 36.5% split, with traders assigning the balance to the most probable single-degree bins given normal forecast uncertainty of ±1–2°C this far ahead.

**No major shifts have emerged in the latest 24–48 hours; guidance remains stable ahead of the 12th.** Resolution will hinge on the official AEMET station reading (Retiro or Barajas), which records the highest instantaneous or hourly value. Continued sunny, dry conditions support the current market consensus, while any unexpected increase in cloudiness or wind would be required to push probabilities toward lower outcomes.

**Persistent southwest monsoon activity is the dominant factor capping maximum temperatures in Manila for August 12, 2026, keeping trader-implied probabilities centered on 29–31 °C.** 

Official PAGASA guidance forecasts a 25–30 °C or 25–32 °C range for Metro Manila under cloudy skies with 60–90 % rain chance from scattered thunderstorms and monsoon rains, consistent with recent observed maxima of 28.7–30.2 °C amid widespread cloud cover. AccuWeather’s broader 29–32 °C envelope and the absence of clear-sky breaks or tropical cyclone influences support the secondary clustering at 29 °C and 31 °C, while lower odds on 32 °C+ reflect limited intensification potential before the next model update. Traders are effectively pricing the monsoon’s ongoing suppression of peak temperatures rather than any anomalous warming.

Historical August climatology shows mean highs near 32–33 °C, underscoring the anomalous warmth captured in the latest model guidance.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Weak monsoon currents across Pakistan, as noted in recent Pakistan Meteorological Department updates, are keeping Karachi temperatures near or slightly below seasonal norms, with August averages around 31–32°C. AccuWeather and long-term climatology indicate daily highs typically range 31–33°C during this period, influenced by high humidity, variable cloud cover, and limited rainfall that prevents strong daytime heating. Model consensus supports this range for August 13, with no major heatwave or intensified monsoon surge expected in the next 48 hours. These conditions explain the market concentration around 32–33°C outcomes, while slight upward or downward shifts would require revised short-term forecasts from official agencies.
